text:
Maya Chen: FYI just got an escalated ticket from Acme-Search. They started seeing a 400 from our embeddings endpoint: "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024" but only for a subset of requests. Customer says it started after they rolled out a client lib update. attaching snippet from their logs.

Acme log:
```
2026-03-14T16:22:11Z ERROR embedding_service: request failed tenant=acme-9876 user=svc-search err=dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024 cache_key=tenant:acme-9876:model:open-embed-v1:prefix:tda3a
```

They also report intermittent latency spikes (~800ms->2s) and increased token billing for the same traffic. Opening thread to triage. @Jordan @Priya any immediate ideas?

Jordan Lee: thanks @Maya. Can you confirm whether the failing requests are cache-hits or misses? The log shows a cache_key but that might be generated before hit check. Also need example request payload (text lengths) and what client lib version they updated to.

Maya Chen: customer provided a repro curl and the client version: `acme-embed-client v1.3.1`. curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-v1","input":["search tokenization sample"],"tenant":"acme-9876"}'
```

They said the same request sometimes works and sometimes errors. No other fields set.

Priya Desai: interesting — this smells like cache key collision across tenants due to client-side prefix truncation we saw in an earlier report. Two possibilities:
- client library switched to a shorter tenant prefix when building cache keys (e.g., truncating tenant id to 8 chars) leading to different tenants mapping to same KV entry; or
- our server-side cache key normalization changed during a deploy and started stripping the model variant suffix for long tenant ids, so cached vectors of a different dimensionality are served.

Priya Desai: can we get the server logs around cache lookups for the exact key `tenant:acme-9876:model:open-embed-v1:prefix:tda3a`? If a mismatched vector was returned from cache we should see a subsequent dimension validation failure.

Alex Kim: I pulled cache audit traces for that time window. Quick summary: there were ~120 requests with that `prefix:tda3a` key in a 10m window. 63 came from tenant `acme-9876`, 51 came from tenant `acme-12-3456` (similar prefix when truncated), 6 were other tenants. Cache returns were mixed: some hits returned earlier 1024-dim vectors (from an older model variant we had earlier), and later the model changed to 1536 dims. So we have cross-tenant contamination via prefix collisions.

SRE Bot: cache.metrics: {"hits": 4821, "misses": 129, "prefix_collisions_detected": 17} (rolling 1h)

Jordan Lee: ohhh. That explains billing spike: when a cache hit returns wrong-dim vector we discard and go to model inference, which is more expensive, and sometimes we fallback to a smaller quantized variant which returns 1024 dims causing the 400 on validation.

Maya Chen: customer asked for repro steps so they can test a fix. I proposed this to them: 1) run two clients with different tenant ids that share the same 8-char prefix, 2) issue identical embedding requests and watch for nondeterministic 400s and latency. They confirmed and can reproduce.

Priya Desai: root cause hypothesis: in `embed-cache` keying we started using `prefix = sha1(tenant_id)[:8]` in v2 of the service at deploy time 2026-03-14T15:50:00Z to reduce key length. That was a mistake because shorter digests increase accidental collisions across tenants with similar ids. We should revert to 16 hex chars or include full tenant id.

Alex Kim: PR ready to revert key derivation and to add tenant scoping explicitly: small patch below (python snippet):
```
# before (v2)
def make_cache_key(tenant_id, model):
    p = hashlib.sha1(tenant_id.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
    return f"tenant:{p}:model:{model}:prefix:{p[:4]}"

# after (patch)
def make_cache_key(tenant_id, model):
    p = hashlib.sha1(tenant_id.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
    return f"tenant:{tenant_id}:model:{model}:hash:{p}"
```

Alex Kim: Also adding runtime validation: if cached vector dim != model.expected_dim then log and increment a `cache_dim_mismatch` counter and treat as miss. That makes failures observable (but will still trigger extra inferences).

Jordan Lee: we should also add a short-term mitigation: for canary we can set the cache TTL to 0 for the model variant that changed dims temporarily to flush bad entries, or add a migration job to scan keys with that short hash and evict those that map to multiple tenant ids. Which is faster?

Priya Desai: eviction job is safer. TTL=0 will cause large spike to inference (customer already seeing issues). We can run a targeted evict for keys where same `prefix` seen with >1 tenant mapping. Alex, can you run a scan + evict in staging then run small canary in prod?@SRE Bot schedule:evict-collisions --pattern "*prefix:tda3a*"

SRE Bot: scheduled: evict-collisions job queued on prod-runner-3, estimated run 2m.

Billing Bot: note: customer reported duplicate higher token usage; recommend issuing a transient credit up to $250 for the noise while we remediate. Need approval from finance.

Maya Chen: I'll request the credit, and inform customer about the planned targeted eviction + patch timeline. Estimated fix: targeted evict -> scan+patch deploy -> 48h monitor.

Alex Kim: ran the staging scan script and found 213 keys with collisions mapping to 7 tenants. Kicked off evict in prod at 16:58. Patch PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/embed-cache/pulls/214 (link).

Deploy Bot: canary deploy started for embed-cache revert (PR 214) on prod namespace canary-a at 2026-03-14T17:05:12Z

SRE Bot: post-evict metrics: prefix_collisions_detected -> 0, cache.misses jumped from 129->341 during eviction window then normalized after canary.

Maya Chen: Customer confirmed at 17:40 that the 400s stopped and latency returned to baseline. They ran their two-client repro and saw no more nondeterministic failures.

Jordan Lee: follow-ups: 1) add unit test for cache key uniqueness (tenant collision scenarios), 2) add `cache_dim_mismatch` alert to paging rules, 3) run a keyspace audit monthly. I'll file tickets.

Priya Desai: thanks everyone. I'll coordinate release to full prod after 24h stable canary and then close the support escalation. Maya, please confirm credit request status.

Maya Chen: credit request submitted to finance@redwood for $200, billing approved pending SOW note. Closing loop once final deploy completes. :white_check_mark:

Alex Kim: postmortem note: misconfiguration + key-length optimization created a class of collision-driven cache contamination. We'll avoid aggressive truncation and prefer explicit tenant scoping in keys.

Maya Chen: marking resolved for now. If customer sees any regression reopen.

[system message] Thread archived by Maya Chen at 2026-03-14T18:01:39Z
